item.title: Gambia signs four solar PPAs totalling 232 MW
item.dc:creator: Patrick Jowett
item.description:
The Gambia’s state-owned utility has inked four large-scale solar power purchase agreements (PPAs) since late October, with battery storage included in each project.

The post Gambia signs four solar PPAs totalling 232 MW appeared first on pv magazine Global.

item.title: Norwegian IPP shifts South African solar project to corporate buyers
item.dc:creator: Brian Publicover
item.description:
Norwegian independent power producer (IPP) Scatec said it plans to withdraw a 288 MW solar project from South Africa’s public renewables procurement program and sell it into the country’s growing corporate power market instead.

The post Norwegian IPP shifts South African solar project to corporate buyers appeared first on pv magazine Global.

item.title: Rare periods of low PV generation can be managed with storage
item.dc:creator: Brian Publicover
item.description:
The German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin) says that batteries could help manage shortfalls in solar and wind generation, while underground storage of green hydrogen could provide backup during prolonged periods of low renewable output.

The post Rare periods of low PV generation can be managed with storage appeared first on pv magazine Global.

item.title: Spain could reach 10 GW of batteries by 2030, but bankability remains the major challenge
item.dc:creator: Emiliano Bellini
item.description: The hybridization of solar PV plants, the evolution of arbitrage and ancillary services revenues, the future capacity market, and the financing of energy storage projects were the focus of a roundtable organized by pv magazine at Genera 2026. Experts anticipate strong growth in the Spanish market, though they warn of administrative hurdles, the lack of a revenue track record, and the complexity of managing these new assets. item.title: India adds 11.2 GW of rooftop PV capacity in first nine months of 2026
item.dc:creator: Uma Gupta
item.description:
India’s residential segment accounted for more than 95% of rooftop solar additions in the third quarter of 2026, driven by the government’s PM Surya Ghar program. Cumulative installed rooftop PV capacity reached 32 GW by the end of September.
